record.context_brief: Boundary concentration in dimensions at least 6
record.original_question: Consider sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega, possibly with nontrivial topology, whose profile has boundary concentration in the sense suggested by an ansatz of the form u_lambda approximately equals u_0 - sum_j W_{mu_j(lambda), xi_j(lambda)}. Is it possible to construct such boundary-concentrating solutions at a fixed parameter lambda >= 0 in dimensions N >= 6?

evidence.quote: In [43, 61], the boundary concentration of sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) has been constructed as lambda -> 0 in dimension N >= 7.

Open question 8: In a general bounded domain Omega, if necessary, it could have nontrivial topology, is it possible to construct boundary concentration of sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem (1.1) at a fixed parameter lambda >= 0 in dimensions N >= 6?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth domain (possibly with nontrivial topology) and consider the Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$ -\Delta u = \lambda u + |u|^{2^*-2} u \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega, $$
where $2^* = 2N/(N-2)$ is the critical Sobolev exponent. For $\mu > 0$ and $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^N$, let
$$ W_{\mu,\xi}(x) = \alpha_N \left( \frac{\mu}{\mu^2 + |x-\xi|^2} \right)^{(N-2)/2} $$
denote the standard Aubin–Talenti bubbles (with the normalizing constant $\alpha_N = (N(N-2))^{(N-2)/4}$ that makes $W_{\mu,\xi}$ a positive solution of $-\Delta W = W^{2^*-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$).

Fix $N \ge 6$ and a parameter $\lambda \ge 0$ (in the admissible range so that $-\Delta - \lambda$ is coercive on $H_0^1(\Omega)$). Question: Does there exist a sign-changing solution $u_\lambda \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ of the above problem of the form
$$ u_\lambda \;\approx\; u_0 \;-\; \sum_{j=1}^{k} W_{\mu_j(\lambda),\,\xi_j(\lambda)}, $$
where $u_0$ is a fixed (positive or sign-changing) solution of the same equation, $k \ge 1$, $\mu_j(\lambda) \to 0$, and the concentration points $\xi_j(\lambda)$ approach the boundary $\partial\Omega$ (i.e. $\mathrm{dist}(\xi_j(\lambda), \partial\Omega) \to 0$)?

Equivalently: construct sign-changing solutions of the Brezis–Nirenberg problem exhibiting boundary concentration at a fixed value of $\lambda \ge 0$ in dimensions $N \ge 6$.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing constructions of boundary-concentrating sign-changing solutions of the Brezis–Nirenberg problem have been carried out in dimensions $N \ge 7$ in the regime $\lambda \to 0$. The case of a fixed parameter $\lambda \ge 0$ in dimensions $N \ge 6$ on a general bounded domain (possibly with nontrivial topology) is listed as an open question in recent work surveying the problem, and no construction was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis-Nirenberg problems: open questions and new results in dimension six
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary concentration of sign-changing solutions has been constructed as lambda -> 0 in dimension N >= 7.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results address only lambda -> 0 and N >= 7, and the fixed-lambda case in N >= 6 is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Nodal solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem in dimension 6
status_evidence.snippet: Sign-changing solutions blowing up at points in Omega as lambda approaches a suitable value lambda_0>0 in dimension 6.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions in N=6 are known for interior blow-up at suitable lambda, but not for boundary concentration at fixed lambda.
